sections.html: French uses the same 26 letters as English, but they are pronounced differently. Knowing the letter names lets you spell your name, an email address or a street name — something you will do constantly in France or Québec.

sections.heading: The letters and their names
sections.html:
Letter Sounds like (approx.) Letter Sounds like (approx.)
A ah N enn
B bay O oh
C say P pay
D day Q kü (lips rounded, like "ee" with pursed lips)
E uh (like the "e" in "the") R air (throaty R)
F eff S ess
G zhay (like the "s" in "measure") T tay
H ahsh U ü (say "ee" with rounded lips)
I ee V vay
J zhee W doo-bluh-vay ("double V")
K kah X eeks
L ell Y ee-grek ("Greek i")
M emm Z zed

sections.heading: The tricky pairs for English speakers
sections.html:
• E (uh) vs I (ee): an English speaker naturally says "ee" for E. In French, I is "ee".
  • G (zhay) vs J (zhee): they are reversed compared to English.
  • U has no English equivalent. Say "ee", keep your tongue where it is, and round your lips as if to whistle.
  • R is pronounced at the back of the throat, close to a light gargle.
  • W is literally "double V", not "double U".

sections.heading: Spelling aloud
sections.html:
When spelling, the French say: - deux L / double L for "ll" (e.g. Gilles: G - I - deux L - E - S) - majuscule = capital letter, minuscule = lowercase - trait d'union = hyphen, apostrophe = apostrophe - For email: arobase = @, point = dot, tiret = dash, tiret bas = underscore

Examples - Comment ça s'écrit ? — How is that spelled? - Martin : M - A - R - T - I - N. - Mon adresse, c'est paul point durand arobase mail point com. — paul.durand@mail.com

sections.heading: Basic sounds of the vowels inside words
sections.html:
Letter Usual sound in words Example
a "ah" papa
e (no accent) "uh" or silent le, petite
i / y "ee" lit, stylo
o "oh" moto
u "ü" tu, lune

exercises.prompt: Write how you would say these letters in French using the approximate sounds above: G, J, E, I, U, W, Y.
exercises.answer: G = *zhay*, J = *zhee*, E = *uh*, I = *ee*, U = *ü*, W = *doo-bluh-vay*, Y = *ee-grek*.

exercises.prompt: Spell these names aloud (write out the letter names): *Hugo*, *Julie*, *Yves*.
exercises.answer: Hugo: *ahsh – ü – zhay – oh*. Julie: *zhee – ü – ell – ee – uh*. Yves: *ee-grek – vay – uh – ess*.

exercises.prompt: How do you say "@" and "." when giving an email address?
Which two letters are "reversed" compared to English pronunciation?
